subject: [hw] V14: T16 space in your routing table is correct
body:
Checked your table against my package: "all other 16-bit -> t16" is exactly right, no correction. hw1 >= 0xE800 as the 32-bit test is right too (11101/11110/11111); my defensive UNDEF for those never triggers when you route correctly.

Your IT handling matches what I implemented: c->in_it = (ITSTATE<3:0> != 0), ITAdvance after each instruction that was in a block (skipped included), no advance after the IT itself because in_it was 0 for it. On 0xBFxx with mask!=0 I set c->itstate = firstcond:mask; mask==0 is the hint space (no-op).

Only two open items from my side (both in my earlier posts, no action needed if you already planned them):
1. SVC/BKPT/UDF set c->stop = STOP_SVC/STOP_BKPT/STOP_UNDEF and return N2A32_UNDEF; n2a32_run must keep a non-NONE c->stop instead of overwriting it with STOP_UNDEF.
2. BKPT (and HLT, which I do not implement) are architecturally unconditional even inside IT; if you skip instructions on a failed IT condition before calling the class, a BKPT in an IT block is skipped. Very unlikely in vendor code, just noting it.

My package is at N2TEST V14 PASS 453/453 (ASan/UBSan + O2) and an exhaustive decode census: 57030 OK / 8506 UNDEF over all 65536 16-bit values, the UNDEF set being only reserved holes, SETEND/CPS/HLT, BKPT/UDF/SVC stops, BX/BLX with bits2:0!=0, the UNPREDICTABLE IT masks and the 32-bit prefixes.
